title: The map in the second variable is natural in the first variable.
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a site and $A$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Work in a universe of modules in which weak sheafification of abelian presheaves exists and sheafification equivalences are exactly locally bijective maps; assume forgetting commutative rings to rings preserves $J$-sheaves. Let $M,M',N,N'$ be sheaves of $A$-modules and $f:M\to M'$, $g:N\to N'$ be $A$-linear sheaf morphisms [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $a$ denote module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], and write $P(M,N)(U)=M(U)\otimes_{A(U)}N(U)$ for the presheaf tensor product with factorwise restrictions [def-pur-presheaf-tensor-product], so $M\otimes_A N=aP(M,N)$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Define $f\otimes\mathrm{id}_N$ to be $a$ applied to the presheaf map $x\otimes y\mapsto f_U(x)\otimes y$, and $\mathrm{id}_M\otimes g$ to be $a$ applied to the presheaf map $x\otimes y\mapsto x\otimes g_U(y)$. These formulas use the module tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Then, as morphisms $M\otimes_A N\to M'\otimes_A N'$, we have
$$
(\mathrm{id}_{M'}\otimes g)\circ(f\otimes\mathrm{id}_N)
=(f\otimes\mathrm{id}_{N'})\circ(\mathrm{id}_M\otimes g).
$$
Thus the map in the second tensor variable is natural in the first variable. No flatness assumption or equality between the site, ring and module universes is imposed.

proof.text: Write $p_f^N:P(M,N)\to P(M',N)$ and $q_g^M:P(M,N)\to P(M,N')$ for the maps with section formulas $x\otimes y\mapsto f_U(x)\otimes y$ and $x\otimes y\mapsto x\otimes g_U(y)$. The bilinear universal property of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] defines these section maps. Applied to the underlying module presheaves of $M,N,N'$, [lem-route-site-tensor-second-map-naturality] says exactly that the sections of $q_g^M$ commute with tensor restrictions, with the target scalar action restricted along $A(U)\to A(V)$. Apply it also with $M'$ for $q_g^{M'}$. For $p_f^N$, the restriction formula in [def-pur-presheaf-tensor-product] gives, along $V\to U$, $f_U(x)|_V\otimes y|_V=f_V(x|_V)\otimes y|_V$, by restriction naturality of the sheaf morphism $f$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Both maps are linear over $A(U)$ after restricting target scalars; uniqueness in the tensor universal property extends this equality from pure tensors. The same argument with $N'$ constructs $p_f^{N'}$.

proof.text: Fix $U\in\mathcal C$. The section maps of $q_g^{M'}\circ p_f^N$ and $p_f^{N'}\circ q_g^M$ are $A(U)$-linear maps from $M(U)\otimes_{A(U)}N(U)$ to $M'(U)\otimes_{A(U)}N'(U)$. Their values on $x\otimes y$ are respectively $f_U(x)\otimes g_U(y)$ and $f_U(x)\otimes g_U(y)$. Apply the pure-tensor extensionality clause of [lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-hom-currying] with $R=A(U)$ and target module $M'(U)\otimes_{A(U)}N'(U)$. Thus the section maps agree for every $U$, and hence $q_g^{M'}\circ p_f^N=p_f^{N'}\circ q_g^M$ as presheaf morphisms.

proof.text: Apply the module-sheafification functor $a$ of [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] to the presheaf equality in step 2. Its composition law gives $a(q_g^{M'})\circ a(p_f^N)=a(p_f^{N'})\circ a(q_g^M)$. By [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] the objects are precisely the tensor sheaves, and by the explicit definitions in the statement the four arrows are $\mathrm{id}_{M'}\otimes g$, $f\otimes\mathrm{id}_N$, $f\otimes\mathrm{id}_{N'}$, and $\mathrm{id}_M\otimes g$. This is the required equality. In the attached Lean signature, composition is written in diagrammatic order $\gg$, so this is exactly siteSheafTensorSecondMap_naturality.
